correctness.rationale: For all k>=3 and r>=3, the binary-edge-status map on k-uniform loose r-cycles has exact mixed-edge transfer M=[[q-1,q],[q,q-1]], q=2^(k-2), with eigenvalues B=2^(k-1)-1 and -1. Definite edges force both core bits and private vertices, so a prescribed status word has fiber equal to the product of constrained mixed-run matrix powers; all mixed has trace M^r=B^r+(-1)^r. Adjacently opposing forced colors yield zero. For >=2 definite edges, bound each entry by (B^ell+1)/2 and use m_a m_b<=m_(a+b) to obtain strict runner-up separation from the 2r single-definite words with fiber (B^(r-1)+(-1)^(r-1))/2. T cyclic status adjacency matrix eigenvalues 1,1±sqrt2 reproduce known smooth-word count. Independently enumerated all vertex subsets and output-word fibers for k=3,r=3..5; k=4,r=3..4; k=5,r=3; k=6,r=3: all exact fibers, maximum and runner-up multiplicities match. Finite runs corroborate rather than prove all r,k.
residual_risks: A potential issue in comparing count formulas was excluded: output status word adjacency for r>=3 is cyclic and full words have positive transfer for mixed runs. The observation-count sequence is prior work; that component is not claimed original.
